messages:
morgan: quick sync — can we pick a single precedence rule for routing when both a signed assertion (x-signed-assertion) and user-agent inference are present? canary rollout slated for tomorrow morning :eyes:
jamie: do you mean the case where they disagree on tenant/priority? or also when signed assertion is present but missing some claims?
alex: i vote: verified signed assertion should win if signature + ttl + nonce check out. otherwise fall back to UA inference. simple rule reduces surprises for enterprise customers.
karen: +1 but add telemetry. we need a counter for 'signed_assertion_used' vs 'ua_inferred' and a tag for why we fell back (expired, invalid sig, missing claim). will be critical for rollback decisions.
greg: security note: signed assertions must be validated against our signing keyset (KMS/HSM). also require a nonce replay check for the last 5 mins to avoid reuse. UA inference should never be treated as authoritative for high-trust routes.
jamie: from a console/rollout UX POV, we should surface these metrics per route:
- pct_routed_by_signed_assertion
- pct_routed_by_ua_inference
- fallback_reasons (invalid_sig, expired, missing_claim)
so SRE/product can judge health during canary.
alex: draft of routing pseudo-config for runtime:```
route "api.v1.generate" {
  match: path("/v1/generate")
  precedence: ["signed_assertion", "client_tag", "ua_inference"]
  signed_assertion_check: { verify: true, required_claims: ["tenant_id"], ttl_seconds: 300 }
  telemetry: { emit_route_source_label: true }
}
```
morgan: sounds good. two open questions: billing mapping and quota enforcement when we fall back to UA (inferred tenant). do we bill the inferred tenant or put under anonymous quota?
akex: (alex) — suggest billing precedence: if verified assertion contains tenant_id -> bill there. else annotate request as "inferred_tenant:<id>" and charge under a special fallback quota bucket, record detailed audit entry. customers can opt-in to allow inferred billing via contract.
karen: add telemetry snippet to runtime so metrics are consistent:```
meta.routing_source = verified ? "signed-assertion" : "ua-inference"
metrics.increment("routing.choice", { source: meta.routing_source, reason: fallback_reason || "none" })
logs.audit("routing_decision", { src: meta.routing_source, tenant: meta.tenant_id || "inferred:"+meta.inferred_tenant })
```
jamie: also: during canary, add alert if signed_assertion_pct < 95% for routes that previously were 100% signed. and a dashboard tile that shows both absolute counts and pct so product can see if canary degrades auth upstream. :shipit:
morgan: ok next steps:
- alex/greg implement verification + nonce check in runtime (priority P0)
- infra to add metrics + labels (karen)
- jamie to add dashboard tiles and canary alerts
- discuss billing fallback policy with finance by EOD
I'll follow up in the rollout doc with exact query names and ID tags. thanks everyone.
infra-bot: deploy-preview created for branch feature/signed-assertion-routing (build #4287). test cluster available at https://ci.redwood.example/4287 :white_check_mark:
jamie: i'll validate metrics once preview is up, pinging @morgan when done.
